industry.why: Neutral, carried, with the sector rows doing the work: Renewable energy equipment and Test and measurement go to D this week and Electrical equipment, Flow control and Building technology hold D, against Distributors, Diversified groups, Engineered components and Industrial services at C. Danske (26-Nov) has automation data points turning up (Rockwell, Siemens Digital Industries) as data-centre installers peak (Bravida Sell; Kristell, 22-Nov) and Kepler (26-Nov) likes cables (Prysmian) and testing; Goldman's cyclical call names Technology, Retailers and Aerospace and Defence, not capital goods. Relative strength D (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; C prior). Three live holdings (Arteche, IMCD, Sdiptech; 12.93 points). Counter-case for D: the tape and the capital-spending unwind; for B: the automation turn. To D on relative strength F with a hyperscaler guide cut read.

sector.why: Neutral, carried: diversification is the simple, proven profile the regime pays for, against cyclical capital goods into a growth scare and small acquirers that a credit crack hurts first; relative strength B (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; B prior). One live holding, Sdiptech (5.76%); Pool name Schouw. Neutral by judgement.

geography.why: Neutral, carried. No Swedish survey and no Riksbank reading reached the pack; the Swedish evidence is sector-level (Nordic small and mid caps de-rating, HMS Networks a buy after one of the largest multiple contractions in the Nordics, Swedish niche game publishers down 4%; Danske, 22 and 26-Nov), which the Fragility row carries. Four live holdings are Swedish (Avanza 5.30%, Elekta 3.98%, Hexatronic 4.89%, Sdiptech 5.76%; 19.93 points, 39% of invested weight), judged in component 5 and amendment 10. Relative strength is not graded by country.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
